noveltyJustification: All nine findings are new: the two registration points, the builder-table entry, the env prefixes, the roster requirement, the alias-plus-thinking pair, the recursion guard, the three audit tables, the exit mapping and the stress fixture had no prior capture.
keyQuestions: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
What does Vibe read from the working directory and ~/.vibe/, and what would a generated repo-root .vibe/ mirror contain?
For each cli-opencode surface this repository uses, does Vibe have an equivalent, a partial equivalent or none, and what would porting take?
What would a cli-mistral-vibe deep-loop executor kind need, and is ACP a better dispatch surface than print mode?

label: A new kind registers in EXECUTOR_KINDS and the zod enum plus EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT; for Vibe the honest fields are model, sandboxMode, timeoutSeconds and liveTools, not reasoningEffort.

The command builder is a LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS entry: vibe -p prompt with --model alias, --agent profile, --output text, --output-dir, --max-turns, --time-limit, --workdir and --trust, stdin closed.
The env allowlist is per kind; Vibe needs VIBE_ and MISTRAL_ prefixes or a dispatched run reports a missing credential, the same failure cli-pi records for LLMGATEWAY_.
A closed model roster is mandatory because --model takes an alias config may not define; a VIBE_SUPPORTED_MODELS list plus isVibeModelAllowed follows the PI and DSH patterns.

The roster must pair alias with expected thinking level: Vibe has no reasoning flag, so honouring the DeepSeek/GLM max pin requires a model row with thinking max and an executor that rejects other aliases.
The recursion guard is generic: adding the kind to the dispatch-stack stamp makes vibe-dispatches-vibe refused before spawn, with no Vibe-specific code.

Dispatch-audit recognition extends three tables: sandbox-is-OS-boundary false (no sandbox flag), web-search policy inherit (no switch), and no session-env entry until a Vibe session id variable is observed.
Vibe's 0/1/2/3/4 exit taxonomy maps onto audit outcome classes, with 3 meaning stopped-without-finishing and therefore scoreable partial work, not success.
Stress coverage needs one adapter fixture under runtime/tests/stress/cli-adapter plus a receipt assertion beside the existing fan-out pwd, stderr, in-process prompt and audit receipt tests.
